content.title: About
content.content: Molasses cookie is a soft, aromatic biscuit made from wheat flour, butter, sugar and molasses. Molasses gives the cookie its dark color and a rich caramel‑to‑honey flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Molasses is a by‑product of sugar production from cane or beet and is rich in minerals and B‑vitamins.
The dark hue of the cookie comes from the high melasse content, which contains iron, calcium and magnesium.
Traditionally these cookies are made in colder regions where molasses was used as a natural sweetener during winter.
Molasses cookies are often served with tea or coffee, as their sweetness pairs well with bitter drinks.
In some countries molasses is considered a healthier alternative to refined sugar because of its lower glycemic index.

items.title: Rich in minerals
items.content: Molasses provides iron, calcium, magnesium and potassium, supporting blood, bone and muscle function.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: The dark color indicates the presence of polyphenols, which help combat free radicals.

items.title: Lower glycemic impact
items.content: Molasses has a lower glycemic index than regular sugar, which may reduce sharp blood‑glucose spikes.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: The cookie offers a quick source of energy thanks to its blend of carbohydrates and a modest amount of fat.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: A small amount of dietary fiber in the cookie aids normal digestive function.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Despite a lower glycemic index, molasses still contains a significant amount of sugar, so consumption should be moderate.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: The cookie contains gluten, making it unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Molasses cookies are relatively calorie‑dense; portion control is advised, especially for weight management.

items.title: Potential heavy‑metal traces
items.content: Some batches of molasses may contain trace amounts of lead or cadmium; choose reputable suppliers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Molasses cookies can be enjoyed as a snack, added to yogurt, ice cream, or used in dessert recipes. They pair well with nuts, dried fruit, and cream cheese.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cookies in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life, keep them in the refrigerator to prevent softening from moisture.
